inline_comments.comment: The `clear()` function does not call `commonClear()` (from `../common/commonDb.js`), which resets shared accessibility metadata — `accTitle`, `accDescription`, and `diagramTitle`. Every other diagram that uses these fields (e.g., block, packet) imports and calls `commonClear()` at the start of its own `clear()`. Because `db.ts` exposes `setAccTitle`, `setAccDescription`, and `setDiagramTitle`, those values can be set by a parsed diagram. Without calling `commonClear()`, stale metadata from a previous render will bleed into the next one. Fix: import `{ clear as commonClear } from '../common/commonDb.js'` and call `commonClear()` at the top of `clear()`.

The `fontFamily` default value has a dangling closing double-quote: `'trebuchet ms",verdana,arial,sans-serif'`. The resulting CSS is `font-family: trebuchet ms",verdana,arial,sans-serif;`, which is invalid because the multi-word font name is not properly quoted. Browsers will reject `trebuchet ms"` and fall through to `verdana`. The correct value should be `'"trebuchet ms",verdana,arial,sans-serif'` (matching how other mermaid diagrams format font stacks).

The TREE_VIEW lexer rule matches the literal string `"treeView"` (8 chars). JISON uses a longest-match rule: for input `treeView-beta`, the pattern `[\S]+` matches 12 characters and beats the 8-character `"treeView"` literal. This means `treeView-beta` is tokenized as a TEXT token, not TREE_VIEW, and `start: TREE_VIEW body` never matches, producing a parse error. The PR description and example code both use `treeView-beta` as the diagram type (consistent with the `-beta` suffix convention used by `packet-beta` and `block-beta`). The detector also accepts `treeView-beta` via `/^\s*treeView/`. The lexer rule should be `"treeView-beta"` to match the intended syntax, or the grammar should explicitly handle an optional `-beta` suffix.

This commented-out lexer rule (`// \%\%[^\ n]*\n /* skip comments */`) is dead code that was never enabled. It should be removed rather than left as a comment; if comment syntax support is planned for a follow-up, that can be tracked in an issue.

`processNode(root)` is called with `root = auxRoot`, the virtual root node (name `'/'`, level `-1`). This causes a `'/'` text label to be rendered as the first visible node in every diagram, which is not reflected in the PR example and appears unintentional. The auxiliary root exists only to provide a stable parent for top-level nodes during parsing. The renderer should iterate over `root.children` and call `processNode` on each, rather than rendering `root` itself. Additionally, `drawNode` draws a horizontal connector line for `auxRoot` starting at `x = 0 - config.rowIndent` (a negative value), which is not compensated for by the viewBox offset on line 118.

The viewBox left offset is `-${config.lineThickness / 2}` (default: `-0.5`). The comment says this accounts for lines at x=0. However, `drawNode` draws the horizontal connector for depth-0 nodes from `x = indent - config.rowIndent = 0 - 10 = -10`, which extends well outside the `-0.5` offset. The connector line for the root node is clipped. If the virtual root rendering issue (above) is fixed by skipping `auxRoot`, the shallowest nodes will be at depth=1 with `indent = rowIndent + paddingX`, so their connectors start at a positive x, and the only negative-x concern comes from the half-thickness of the stroke, which the current offset does handle.

`drawNode` is defined inside `drawTree` and always called with the same `elem` and `config` values that are already in the enclosing scope. Passing them as parameters is redundant — they could simply be referenced from the closure, leaving only `node` and `depth` as parameters. This would make the intent of the inner function clearer and reduce noise at every call site.

`BBox` is an optional field on `Node` that is set by `positionLabel` during rendering and then read back by `processNode` using a non-null assertion (`node.BBox!`). Storing rendering state inside the parsed data model couples the two layers and makes it harder to re-render without re-parsing. A cleaner approach is to maintain a `Map<number, BBox>` keyed by node id inside the renderer, keeping the `Node` type as a pure data structure.

`DiagramDetector` and `DiagramLoader` are imported on line 1, and `ExternalDiagramDefinition` is imported on line 2 — both from the same module `'../../diagram-api/types.js'`. These should be merged into a single `import type { DiagramDetector, DiagramLoader, ExternalDiagramDefinition }` statement.

The `.treeView-node-label` CSS rule sets `font-size` and `font-family` but omits `fill`. In SVG, text color is controlled by the `fill` attribute/property, not `color`. Without an explicit `fill`, text inherits whatever fill is set higher in the SVG tree, which can produce invisible text on dark themes. Consider adding `fill: currentColor` or a theme-appropriate variable.

general_comments.comment: There are no unit or integration tests anywhere in the treeView directory. The PR checklist marks tests as completed, but the explorer found no `.spec.ts` or `.test.ts` files. Given the parsing subtleties (indentation-as-level, newline handling, stack-based parent resolution), and the multi-step rendering pipeline (label sizing → BBox storage → line positioning → viewBox calculation), test coverage is especially important here. At minimum, parser tests for same-depth siblings, nested nodes, and edge cases (empty body, single node) should be added, along with renderer snapshot tests for the SVG output.
